summary: A Pulse room message that enumerates several requests (« 1. … 2. … ») is split by the host and run one request after the other, each as its own admitted event; a question stops the run and the dialogue coordinator keeps the rest until the answer (Amine 26/10: « il faut gérer ce genre de demande automatiquement »).
reason: S24 26/10 15:37:50Z: Sadok sent « 1. État su projet zain phase 5\n2. Passe la phase réalisation du projet 20495 a non débuté ». The whole message went to the interpreter as one request and the room answered « Cette demande ne définit pas une commande Pulse admise ».

tests.name: scripts/test-pulse-room-fast-path.cjs
tests.evidence: Sadok's real message is split into two requests run as events <messageId>#1 and #2 of the same conversation, the first carrying the second as queuedRequests; non-enumerated texts (« nom projet …\nclient … », an intro line, one item, 11 items, a time) stay one request; a question stops the run and tells the contact the other request is kept; the answer turn runs the resumeRequests as <messageId>#r1; an older coordinator that keeps nothing makes the room say the rest was not run; in the native room each request gets its own admission (eventRef and text bound), turn and hand-off. Existing cases unchanged.

capabilities.reason: No capability, route or scope change. Each request goes through the same native admission, coordinator scope policy and hand-off as a one-request message.

architecture.reason: Stateless host loop in the existing room adapter; waiting requests live only in the coordinator's conversation state (samantha-ui-playbooks change of the same name). No second router, store, timer or retry.

evidence: Read-only assessment: only the WhatsApp Pulse room adapter changes; no MCP schema, adapter, endpoint or runtime protocol changed.

limitations: Full canonical CI on the final GitHub head remains required.
Queueing behind a question needs the paired playbooks coordinator; before its activation the room says the other requests were not run.
Requests run sequentially in one WhatsApp turn: the reply arrives after the last one (about 30 s each today).
Live proof: Sadok's two-line message answered for both requests in the Pulse room.
rollback: Revert this commit; an enumerated message is again one request.
